scope: Primary sources read by the root agent in addition to the context and verification matrices. No inference calls or pipeline changes.

sources.title: Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents
sources.read_sections: Sections 2.1 to 2.3, Tables 2 and 3, and author README.
sources.finding: The paper compares executable code actions with text/JSON actions in API-Bank and compositional M3ToolEval, using 17 historical models. Python supplies control/data flow and reusable intermediate state; benefits depend on model/task and are not universal.
sources.local_inference: Use code for filtering/aggregation over exact workspace data and bounded observations. Do not migrate every native tool call to code or assume persistent mutable interpreter state is required.
sources.limitations: Different tasks/models/action formats. It does not test bounded Python results or this Luna FHIR team. Our sandbox isolation and source immutability must remain intact.

sources.title: Official OpenAI structured outputs and function calling documentation
sources.read_sections: Structured Outputs versus JSON mode, supported schemas, strict mode, refusal/incomplete-output handling.
sources.finding: JSON mode only establishes parseable JSON; structured outputs and strict function schemas constrain shape. Unsupported schemas can be rejected. Refusals and incomplete generations remain explicit edge cases.
sources.local_inference: Use role-specific typed final schemas and explicit inspection/computation envelopes, while retaining deterministic source, scope and computation-equality validation.
sources.local_transport_review: The private Azure adapter forwards response_format at lines 100 to 102, but public safe_llm_call and BaseAgent._llm_call do not currently expose that argument. Supporting adapter passthrough is not proof that current role outputs are strict or that every planned schema works on the deployed service.
sources.limitations: Normative API guidance, not evidence of semantic correctness or accuracy gain. Validate the pinned transport/schema subset offline and with a small sanity stage included in a future pilot; no API call was made during this research.

sources.title: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Calling Agents in Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)
sources.read_sections: Background, Section 3.2 system architecture and experiment scope.
sources.finding: Its FHIR harness stores retrieved resources in a shared workspace, permits Python schema inspection and computation, and distinguishes a terminal Finish action. It also changes training and the agent harness.
sources.local_inference: The inspection/computation/finalization separation is relevant engineering precedent. RL training and changing base models are outside this Luna repair plan.
sources.limitations: Different models, training and evaluation. Its performance claims do not validate our repairs, and no new training or benchmark migration is proposed.

validation_status: Source-backed design and local trace/provenance evidence are established. Proposed implementation correctness and accuracy gains require the planned offline tests and controlled pilot.
